findings.title: Failed device tagging is cached, allowing device-limit bypass
findings.body: tagDeviceUI adds the device ID to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not remove it when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The first request for a new device after the limit is reached fails authentication, but the cache entry remains for 29 minutes; subsequent requests hit the cache and return nil without a database check, so the unregistered device is authenticated. Set the cache only after a successful write or delete it on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with insert/update
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first counts active devices and then performs the upsert in a separate database session. Concurrent first-time requests from multiple new devices can all observe count below the configured limit and then all insert, causing the active anonymous device count to exceed the limit. If this is intended as a hard cap, enforcement must be atomic, for example via a transaction with locking or a conditional insert.

findings.title: Limit tests do not cover existing-device updates or retry/cache behavior
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that inserting a second new device fails when the store limit is 1. It does not verify that an already-registered device can still be updated after the limit is reached, nor does it exercise the higher-level TagDevice flow where the local cache can bypass the limit. Add coverage for updating an existing device at the limit and for the service-level cache path.
